title: Cross-functional SLO Implementation Sprint Map — 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working doc maps the cross-functional sprints, owners, and dependencies required to implement the 2026 reliability program SLOs across hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It is intended to be actionable for engineering leads, product, platform, and SRE stakeholders.

Scope:
- Implement baseline SLOs (p95 latency, error rate, availability) for three product surfaces: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane.
- Deliver telemetry pipelines, alerting rules, runbooks, and canary rollouts.
- Integrate SLOs into rollout policies and the Console dashboards.
- Excludes long-lead infra capacity procurement (tracked separately).

Goals (measurable):
- Define and publish SLOs and SLIs by 2026-03-31.
- End-to-end telemetry for SLOs in prod for Hosted API by 2026-05-15.
- Canary+rollback integration with Console by 2026-06-15.
- Cross-product runbooks and oncall playbooks published by 2026-06-30.

Success metrics (KRs):
- 95% of requests covered by SLO instrumentation (traces/metrics) in Hosted API.
- Alert noise < 5 actionable alerts/week after tuning in month 1 post-rollout.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) for SLO breaches reduced by 30% vs baseline.

High-level timeline (quarters and sprint buckets):
- Sprint 1 (2026-02-01 to 2026-02-21): SLO definitions, measurement design, ownership matrix.
- Sprint 2 (2026-02-22 to 2026-03-14): Telemetry proto + metrics schema, initial dashboards.
- Sprint 3 (2026-03-15 to 2026-04-04): Ingest pipelines and sampling strategy; test harness.
- Sprint 4 (2026-04-05 to 2026-04-25): Alert rules + runbook drafts; tabletop exercises.
- Sprint 5 (2026-04-26 to 2026-05-16): Canary rollout for Hosted API; monitor and iterate.
- Sprint 6 (2026-05-17 to 2026-06-06): Console integration and cross-product dashboards.
- Sprint 7 (2026-06-07 to 2026-06-27): Private/Dedicated parity work and documentation.

Sprint map (workstreams, owners, deliverables):
- Measurement & SLO design (Owner: Maya Thompson; collaborators: Product/Alex, Research/Chen):
  - Deliverables: SLO definitions doc, SLI query library (examples), agreed measurement windows.
  - Acceptance: SLO doc approved by Product and SRE primaries.

- Telemetry & Ingest (Owner: Diego Alvarez; collaborators: infra, observability):
  - Deliverables: Metric schema PR, ingestion pipelines in staging, sampling strategy.
  - Acceptance: End-to-end metric verified in staging; no more than 3% added cardinality overhead.

- Alerting & Runbooks (Owner: Priya Kapoor; collaborators: Support, Oncall leads):
  - Deliverables: Alert rule set, runbook templates, escalation graph.
  - Acceptance: Tabletop test with oncall team passes (scenario-based).

- Console & Rollouts (Owner: Liam O'Neill; collaborators: product-console, release-eng):
  - Deliverables: Dashboard tiles, canary gating integration, rollout policy UI hooks.
  - Acceptance: Canary gating can be triggered and rolled back through Console in staging.

- Private/Dedicated Parity (Owner: Chen Wu; collaborators: private-deployments team):
  - Deliverables: Packaging guide, KMS audit integration, deployment checklist.
  - Acceptance: Customer-simulated private deployment reports SLO signals in Console.

Dependency matrix (key cross-team handoffs):
- Telemetry schema must be finalized before Console integration (Telemetry -> Console).
- Alerting rules require SLI definitions and runbook templates (SLO design -> Alerting).
- Canary rollout requires release-engineering feature flags + infra capacity window (Console -> Release-Eng -> Infra).
- Private parity depends on security/KMS integration (Private -> Security).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: High cardinality metrics will blow up storage and costs.
  - Mitigation: Sampling + aggregation strategy established in Sprint 2; explicit budget control for retention.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from early thresholds.
  - Mitigation: Progressive escalation — start with advisory alerts, tune thresholds in sprint 4, require runbook-run before alert de-escalation.
- Risk: Console rollout regressions affecting customer-facing telemetry.
  - Mitigation: Canary in internal org, shadow mode for 2 weeks, automated rollback on SLO deviation.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync (30min) for owners + SRE leads — cadence: Tuesdays 10:00am PT.
- Bi-weekly demos for exec sponsors (30 min).
- Slack channel: #reliability-slo-2026 for async updates, links to PRs and dashboards.
- Confluence page (linked) will be the single source of truth for SLO docs.

Testing and verification:
- Define test harness for synthetic load to validate p95 latency SLOs (owner: infra-test).
- Run three tabletop incident drills during rollout: pre-canary, mid-rollout, post-rollout.
- Post-mortem template required for any SLO breach with retro within 3 business days.

Rollout playbook (mini):
1) Feature-flag + shadow mode for new SLO signals.
2) Internal canary (10% of traffic, internal org) for 48 hours.
3) Monitor SLO signals and alert counts; if > threshold, rollback feature-flag.
4) Expand to gradual % increases over 7 days with daily checks.
5) Flip to fully enforced with runbook triggers and public dashboard.

Open questions (to resolve in sprint 1):
- What is the canonical measurement window for p95 vs p99 across product surfaces?
- Who signs off on 'severity classification' for SLO breaches (product or SRE)?
- Acceptable additional cost (dollars/month) for 90-day retention of SLO signals?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finish SLO definition draft and circulate for review (owner: Maya).
- Engineering leads to nominate telemetry owners for each product surface (owner: Diego).
- Schedule tabletop drill slot with oncall rotation (owner: Priya).

Notes and context (short):
- This doc intentionally keeps implementation details lightweight; PRs and runbook drafts will live in linked artifacts.
- Goal is a pragmatic, iterative rollout with clear ownership and automated safeguards to reduce blast radius.
